findings.title: getBaseConditions returns unparenthesized OR fragments when only one side applies
findings.body: When only one of auth/filter conditions exists, `getBaseConditions` returns that fragment as-is (lines 74-77). For org and team scope the authorization fragment is a top-level `(A) OR (B)` (reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207), and the eventTypeId filter is a top-level `(X) OR (Y)` (line 106, returned unwrapped by the reduce at 119-122 when it is the only filter). The both-present branch wraps its operands (line 73), but the single-operand branches do not. A caller that composes the result the way the test does, `WHERE ${base} AND <predicate>`, gets `(A) OR ((B) AND <predicate>)` because AND binds tighter than OR, so rows outside the authorized set are returned silently. Nothing in the repo calls this class in production yet (only the integration test imports it), so this is latent. Suggested fix for the failure shown: wrap the single-operand returns in `Prisma.sql\`(${x})\`` (or wrap the OR-producing builders), so `getBaseConditions` always returns a parenthesized predicate.

findings.title: Caching tests were deleted and not replaced
findings.body: The `describe("Caching")` block (both "should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") was removed in this diff, and nothing replaces it. The cache logic is still present and is non-trivial: `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` use `=== undefined` checks (packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:83-95) so a cached `null` filter result is not rebuilt. The removed tests were the only coverage of that behaviour, including the null case, which is now untested. Restore a caching test, or say in the PR why the behaviour no longer needs one.

findings.title: SQL-shape assertions compare fragment text, not the rows they select; NOTHING test uses a copy of the constant
findings.body: Most of the new assertions compare a `Prisma.sql` object to another `Prisma.sql` literal (for example lines 273, 295-299, 332-343, 384-386, 407, 429-431). They pass for any output with the same text and parameter order, and they do not check which rows match. Lines 384-386 also codify the unparenthesized `OR` fragment that is the precedence issue in insightsBooking.ts:75. Only the single `getBaseConditions` case (lines 437-501) runs the SQL against the view. The `NOTHING_CONDITION` on line 10 is a second copy of the production `1=0` (insightsBooking.ts:43), so the 'should return NOTHING' assertions at lines 210 and 245 compare the constant with a copy of itself and would not notice a change to the production value. Consider running the org and team scopes against the database with rows that should be included and excluded, and asserting on the rows returned.

contracts.action: Removal of InsightsBookingService.findMany and the switch to a $queryRaw WHERE fragment
contracts.before_after: Before: findMany() merged its where with AND [authConditions, filterConditions]. After: getBaseConditions() returns a Prisma.Sql fragment that the caller must embed in $queryRaw. The repository has no production caller of this class; the only importer is the integration test.

contracts.action: Org-scope authorization condition rebuilt as Prisma.sql with ANY(array) parameters
contracts.before_after: Before: { OR: [ {teamId in teamIds, isTeamBooking true}, {userId in users, isTeamBooking false} (only when users non-empty) ] }. After: the same two clauses as SQL. teamIds always includes options.orgId so the ANY array is never empty, and the user clause is added only when userIdsFromOrg is non-empty, as before. The sibling team-scope builder uses the same ANY pattern.

contracts.action: Team-scope authorization condition rebuilt as Prisma.sql
contracts.before_after: Before: the userId clause was always present, with `in: []` when the team had no members (which matches nothing). After: the userId clause is omitted when userIdsFromTeam is empty. Matching nothing is the same result, so the rows returned do not change.

contracts.action: Composition of auth and filter fragments in getBaseConditions
contracts.before_after: Before: AND of two where objects, which Prisma parenthesises itself. After: string composition. Both-present case wraps each operand; single-operand cases return the operand unwrapped, which can break precedence when a caller adds further predicates.
contracts.failure_mode: A caller that writes WHERE ${base} AND <predicate> would return rows outside the org/team authorization set. No such caller exists today.

contracts.action: isOrgOwnerOrAdmin role check rewritten from array includes to === comparisons
contracts.before_after: Before: [OWNER, ADMIN].includes(role). After: role === OWNER || role === ADMIN. Same truth table for MembershipRole values.

summary: Reviewed both files in full. The conversion from Prisma where objects to Prisma.sql fragments keeps the same authorization and filter semantics for user, org, team and filter scopes. The view column names used in the raw SQL match the BookingTimeStatusDenormalized view, and all values are bound as parameters. No production code calls InsightsBookingService (only the integration test imports it), so nothing changes for users in this PR. The findings are about the composability of getBaseConditions (a latent precedence hazard), a deleted Caching test block that was not replaced, and assertions that compare SQL text rather than the rows returned. No blockers or fixes. docs/adr/ has no files on the base commit, so there is no ADR to check against.
